note.note:
Action Plan:
1) Arrange in-person clinical assessment: Patient to call the support line today to schedule a face-to-face clinic visit for abdominal examination and further evaluation of worsening lower abdominal pain and associated vaginal spotting/discharge.
2) Perform a urine pregnancy test today: Patient to complete the test today. If positive, she will call back immediately for urgent assessment to rule out ectopic pregnancy.
3) Safety-net advice: If pain worsens, if she cannot keep fluids down, feels faint, develops fever, shoulder-tip pain, or experiences heavy bleeding, she will seek urgent medical attention prior to the scheduled clinic visit.
4) Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
- Reason for visit: Constant lower abdominal (suprapubic, midline) pain, worsening over a few days.
- HPI:
  - Pain: Lower abdomen, midline below the umbilicus; constant; severity ~8/10; worsening over the last few days.
  - Associated symptoms: Light pink vaginal bleeding/spotting; slight vaginal discharge; nausea without vomiting.
  - Bowel: Constipated for about a week last week; now improved/normal.
  - Urinary: No dysuria; no pain or strong smell; frequency unclear; no flank pain reported.
  - Constitutional: No fever reported; no dyspnea; no shoulder-tip pain; no presyncope/syncope.
  - Function: Eating and drinking OK; able to perform daily activities but pain is very uncomfortable.
- Gynecologic/obstetric:
  - Sexually active; last intercourse ~4 days ago.
  - Contraception: Contraceptive implant (Implanon/Nexplanon) inserted ~1 year ago.
  - Menses: Occur but irregular since implant; last menstrual period ~2–3 weeks ago; last period was reported as normal.
  - G0; no prior pregnancies.
  - Pregnancy testing: Last test about 1 month ago (none since pain began).
- Past medical/surgical history: No surgeries reported; no chronic conditions reported.
- Medications: Contraceptive implant in situ; other medications not documented.
- Allergies: Amoxicillin.
- Social: School teacher; lives with husband and husband’s family; no recreational drug use; smoking/alcohol status unclear; no recent travel (last abroad ~1 year ago).

Objective:
- Teleconsultation; no physical examination performed.
- Vitals: Not obtained.
- Investigations today: None obtained during call.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Lower abdominal pain (constant, suprapubic/midline, worsening):
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Undifferentiated acute pelvic pain.
   - Differential diagnosis:
     - Ectopic pregnancy (Medium): Pelvic pain with light bleeding; no recent pregnancy test since symptom onset; implant reduces but does not eliminate risk.
     - Pelvic inflammatory disease (Medium): Pelvic pain with spotting and slight discharge; absence of fever does not exclude.
     - Functional/hemorrhagic ovarian cyst (Medium): Acute pelvic pain with intermenstrual spotting; implant users can develop functional cysts.
     - Acute appendicitis (Low-Medium): Worsening abdominal pain with nausea; atypical location and lack of fever argue against but do not exclude.
     - Urinary tract infection/cystitis (Low): Suprapubic pain possible; no dysuria/fever.
   - Investigations planned: In-person abdominal examination at clinic; urine pregnancy test today (if positive, urgent review to rule out ectopic pregnancy).
   - Treatment planned: None initiated during teleconsult.
   - Relevant referrals: Face-to-face clinic appointment via support line.

2. Vaginal spotting and slight vaginal discharge:
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Abnormal uterine bleeding (intermenstrual spotting).
   - Differential diagnosis:
     - Implanon-related irregular bleeding (possible).
     - Ectopic pregnancy (Medium) or early intrauterine pregnancy with threatened miscarriage (less likely but important to exclude) — pending pregnancy test.
     - Pelvic inflammatory disease (Medium).
     - Functional ovarian cyst (Medium).
   - Investigations planned: Urine pregnancy test today; evaluation during in-person visit.
   - Treatment planned: None initiated during teleconsult.

3. Constipation (last week, now improved):
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Recent constipation, resolved; unlikely sole cause of current pain.
   - Differential diagnosis: Constipation/IBS (less likely given pain persistence despite bowel improvement).
   - Investigations planned: None at present.
   - Treatment planned: None required currently.

4. Nausea without vomiting:
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Mild nausea associated with abdominal/pelvic pain.
   - Differential diagnosis: As per Issue 1 etiologies.
   - Investigations planned: None separate from Issue 1.
   - Treatment planned: None during teleconsult; safety-net provided (seek care if unable to keep fluids down).

5. Contraception/pregnancy status (implant in situ; exclude pregnancy):
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Pregnancy unlikely but must be excluded; ectopic pregnancy risk if pregnant.
   - Differential diagnosis: Ectopic pregnancy (Medium) per DDx.
   - Investigations planned: Urine pregnancy test today; if positive, urgent assessment arranged.
   - Treatment planned: Not applicable unless results indicate.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - No vitals obtained.
  - No abdominal or pelvic examination performed (teleconsult).
  - No pregnancy test result available yet (test planned today).
  - No urinalysis, STI testing, or pelvic ultrasound arranged/documented during this call.
  - Medication list not reconciled beyond contraceptive implant.
  - Smoking and alcohol history unclear.
- Internal conflicts between transcript and DDx: None noted between transcript and DDx.
- Transcript quality: Intermittent audio/clarity issues with several inaudible segments; some responses ambiguous (e.g., urinary frequency, alcohol/smoking).
